title: Happy days after the marriages
introduction: The wedding party arrives at Ayodhya on the exit of Parashu Rama. Yudhaajit, the maternal uncle of Bharata, who came before marriages, now takes Bharata and Shatrughna to his kingdom. Rama and Lakshmana from then on are engaged in the welfare works of their subjects, at the behest of their father. Rama and Seetha will then enter the threshold of their blissful married life.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे सप्तसप्ततितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 77th, and conclusive chapter of Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
गते रामे प्रशांतात्मा रामो दाशरथिर्धनुः |
वरुणायाप्रमेयाय ददौ हस्ते महायशाः
verses.iast:
gate rāme praśānta ātmā rāmo dāśarathiḥ dhanuḥ |
varuṇāya aprameyāya dadau haste mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: On the departure of Rama of Jamadagni, that most glorious Rama of Dasharatha is quietened at heart, and he gave away that longbow of Vishnu into the hand of inimitable Rain-god.
notes: On this longbow and its giving to god of Rain, some discussion is incorporated in the earlier chapter.

glosses.meaning: of Rama of Jamadagni, on the departure of
quietened, at heart, Dasharatha, Rama of

verses.devanagari:
अभिवाद्य ततो रामो वसिष्ठ प्रमुखानृषीन् |
पितरं विह्वलं दृष्ट्वा प्रोवाच रघुनंदनः
verses.iast:
abhivādya tato rāmo vasiṣṭha pramukhān ṛṣīn |
pitaram vihvalam dṛṣṭvā provāca raghunandanaḥ
verses.translation: On paying respects to sage Vashishta and to the other important sages, Rama, the delight of Raghu's lineage, placatingly addressed his agitated father Dasharatha.

verses.devanagari:
जामदग्न्यो गतो रामः प्रयातु चतुरङ्गिगिणी |
अयोध्याभिमुखी सेना त्वया नाथेन पालिता
verses.iast:
jāmadagnyo gato rāmaḥ prayātu catur angiṇī |
ayodhyā abhimukhī senā tvayā nāthena pālitā
verses.translation: "Rama of Jamadagni has gone on his way, you may now order the army under your wardship, for which you are the lord, to move on towards Ayodhya..." So said Rama to his father.

glosses.meaning: Jamadagni, Rama of, gone away [gone on his way]
towards, Ayodhya, let it move on.

verses.devanagari:
4,5 रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा दशरथः सुतम् |
बाहुभ्यां संपरिष्वज्य मूर्ध्नि चाघ्राय राघवम्
गतो राम इति श्रुत्वा हृष्टः प्रमुदितो नृपः |
पुनर्जातं तदा मेने पुत्रमात्मानमेव च
verses.iast:
rāmasya vacanam śrutvā rājā daśarathaḥ sutam |
bāhubhyām sampariṣvajya mūrdhni upāghrāya rāghavam
gato rāma iti śrutvā hṛṣṭaḥ pramudito nṛpaḥ |
punarjātam tadā mene putram ātmānam eva ca
verses.translation: On hearing the words of Rama king Dasharatha hugged his son with both of his arms, and kissed on the forehead of Raghava, and king Dasharatha is gladdened to listen about the departure of Parashu Rama, and then he is further gladdened in deeming that he and his sons took a rebirth.

glosses.meaning: son, Raghava, with both arms, hugged
presumed - presumed to have taken a rebirth.

verses.devanagari:
चोदयामास तां सेनां जगामाशु ततः पुरीम् |
पताकाध्वजिनीं रम्यां तूर्योद्घुष्टनिनादिताम्
सिक्तराजपथां रम्यां प्रकीर्णकुसुमोत्कराम् |
राजप्रवेशसुमुखैः पौरैर्मंगलपाणिभिः
संपूर्णां प्राविशद्राजा जनौघैः समलंकृताम् |
verses.iast:
codayāmāsa tām senām jagāma āśu tataḥ purīm |
patākā dhvajinīm raṃyām tūrya ud ghuṣṭa nināditām
sikta rāja pathā raṃyām prakīrṇa kusuma utkarām |
rāja praveśa sumukhaiḥ pauraiḥ maṅgala pāṇibhiḥ
sampūrṇām prāviśat rājā jana oghaiḥ samalaṅkṛtām |
verses.translation: Then the King Dasharatha ordered that legion to move ahead, and then they all went towards delightful city Ayodhya, whose royal highways are wetted with water, sprinkled with bunches of flowers, decorated with banners and bannerettes up above them, and reverberating with high sounding bugle-horns. Further, those highways are replete with urbanites welcomers who are handling welcoming kits which are golden handy-crates or plates in which lit camphor, fragrant incenses, vermilion powder, flowers to shower on the incomers are arranged, and those highways are well-decorated with throngs of people who are glee-faced at their king's re-entry, and into such an exhilarating city Ayodhya king Dasharatha and his retinue entered.

glosses.meaning: that, legion, ordered to move ahead
welcoming kits, in their hands, with urbanites
into such exhilarating, city Ayodhya, went to

verses.devanagari:
पौरैः प्रत्युद्गतो दूरं द्विजैश्च पुरवासिभिः
पुत्रैरनुगतः श्रीमान् श्रीमद्भिश्च महायशाः |
प्रविवेश गृहं राजा हिमवत्सदृशं प्रियम्
verses.iast:
pauraiḥ prati udgato dūram dvijaiḥ ca pura vāsibhiḥ
putraiḥ anugataḥ śrīmān śrīmadbhiḥ ca mahāyaśāḥ |
praviveśa gṛham rājā himavat sadṛśam priyam
verses.translation: When the citizenry and city-dwelling Brahman-s have received him from a distance, that illustrious king Dasharatha followed by his phenomenal and praiseworthy sons then entered his happy house and home, which is like the lofty and lordly Himalayan palazzo.
notes: 'King entered the house...' is not just an entrance of a character into a scene, but it entails a lot of ceremony called gṛha praveśa 'entering into householder-hood, the second stage of life gārhapatya dharma out of the four stages of living, 1] celibate scholar, 2] householder, 3] repairing to forest or sageship, 4] final release, moksha. pāṇi grahaṇa anantarm kriyamāṇo gṛha praveśaḥ - dk where ceremonies go on for hours together.

glosses.meaning: towards, oppositely, going [people came to receive the king]

verses.devanagari:
ननन्द स्वजनै राजा गृहे कामैः सुपूजितः |
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च सुमध्यमा
वधूप्रतिग्रहे युक्ता याश्चान्या राजयोषितः |
verses.iast:
nananda svajanaiḥ rājā gṛhe kāmaiḥ supūjitaḥ |
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca sumadhyamā
vadhū pratigrahe yuktā yāḥ ca anyā rāja yoṣitaḥ |
verses.translation: In palace king Dasharatha is overjoyed when he is surrounded with his own inmates of palace-chambers, and when his long cherished ambitions have come true, while his queens, Kausalya, Sumitra, and slender waisted Kaikeyi and other wives are overjoyed in the functions of receiving the four brides.
notes: Again this 'receiving bride' is an elaborate variety of fun and games of womenfolk will take place, at which place there is almost no entry to men. For example, name telling. An Indian bride, or the later time wife is supposed to not to call her husband by his name. It is a sacred taboo, and her addressing shall be in genderless, person-less, and numberless hooting, cooing or calling like e jī - o jī - emanḍī - ennango - śuniye so on. To cite one such ceremony it is 'naming game.' Here the bride is compelled to tell the name of her husband, and she will be hesitating to do so, because of her newness to this house or to her husband. After some teasing attempts, she mutters her husband's name, and then only she will be admitted into certain chamber or room. But dwindling are these games, and dampening is that fun, in these days of readymade marriages. Then why Dasharatha shall be overjoyed at these womanly functions, they do all those womanish things... because, Dasharatha wanted his palace to be in festivity, with just one son. But four are forced on him and they too obtained four brides in one go, hence fourfold is his happiness. It may be observed that Kaikeyi is the lone queen with 'beauty' as her attribute, and the problem with her is seeded here alone, saying that enchantment of Dasharatha towards her outweighs his affection to Rama, later.

glosses.meaning: by ambitions, well, reverenced [when his long cherished ambitions have come true]
which of those, other, king's, wives - are there, they

verses.devanagari:
ततः सीतां महाभागामूर्मिलां च यशस्विनीम्
कुशध्वजसुते चोभे जगृहुर्नृपयोषितः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ sītām mahābhāgām ūrmilām ca yaśasvinīm
kuśadhvaja sute ca ubhe jagṛhuḥ nṛpa yoṣitaḥ |
verses.translation: Then the womenfolk of the king welcomed the highly propitious Seetha and the highly fortunate Urmila too, along with both the daughters of Kushadhvaja, namely Maandavi and Shrutakiirti, with pageantry and festivity.

verses.devanagari:
मंगलालापनैर्होमैः शोभिताः क्षौमवाससः
देवतायतनान्याशु सर्वास्ताः प्रत्यपूजयन् |
verses.iast:
maṅgala ālāpanaiḥ homaiḥ śobhitāḥ kṣauma vāsasaḥ
devata āyatanāni āśu sarvāḥ tāḥ pratyapūjayan |
verses.translation: All of the brides and bridegrooms clad in silks promptly worshipped the gods in sanctums to the benedictory chanting of Vedic hymns and Ritual-fires, thus they shone forth like the tongues of Holy Fires of Vedic Altars.
notes: These young couples by themselves are radiant, and they are now clad in radiant silks that glitter wavily like the tongues of fire, and the Ritual-fire s are already there flaring wavily, to the weave-like chanting of Vedic benedictions. With all these waving, flaring, glaring the couples too appeared as the humanly Ritual-fires before the wood burnt Vedic Ritual-fires.

verses.devanagari:
अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांश्च सर्वा राजसुतास्तदा
रेमिरे मुदिताः सर्वा भर्तृभिः सहिता रहः |
verses.iast:
abhivādya abhivādyān ca sarvā rāja sutāḥ tadā
remire muditāḥ sarvā bhar.htṛbhiḥ sahitā rahaḥ |
verses.translation: Then all the princesses paid respects to all of the respectable ones, and they luxuriated in sequestered palace-chambers along with their husbands.
notes: This 'paying respects to respectable elders' is but one line. In reality, the torsos of those that pay respects will be put to test, because they have to 'pay' by bending and touching the feet of elders, each time to each, pāda abhivandana, pai lagoo . And if the girls are from jeans or pants culture, [because days have gone,] they will be fresh and new to bridal sari, which itself will be a weight to carry. And many times we see the young brides falling on the blessing couple because her bridal sari gets entangled in the toes of the bride, and she is not yet ready to manage it. So goes on this parade until their backs are broken.

glosses.meaning: those who are respect worthy, on paying respects to them, also

verses.devanagari:
कृतदाराः कृतास्त्राश्च सधनाः ससुहृज्जनाः
शुश्रूषमाणाः पितरं वर्तयन्ति नरर्षभाः |
verses.iast:
kṛta dārāḥ kṛta astrāḥ ca sa dhanāḥ sa suhṛt janāḥ
śuśrūṣamāṇāḥ pitaram vartayanti nararṣabhāḥ |
verses.translation: And those best men among men, Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata, Shatrughna, who are by now accomplished persons in weaponry and whose marriages have also come to pass, occupied themselves in the welfare of kingdom while assisting their father and moving around with good hearted people.

glosses.meaning: occupied themselves - in welfare of kingdom.

verses.devanagari:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य राजा दशरधः सुतम्
भरतं कैकेयीपुत्रमब्रवीद्रघुनन्दनः |
verses.iast:
kasyacit atha kālasya rājā daśaradhaḥ sutam
bharatam kaikeyī putram abravīt raghunndana |
verses.translation: Then after sometime that king Dasharatha, the legatee of Raghu-s, spoke to his and Kaikeyi's son, Bharata.

verses.devanagari:
अयं केकयराजस्य पुत्रो वसति पुत्रक
त्वां नेतुमागतो वीरो युधाजिन्मातुलस्तव |
verses.iast:
ayam kekaya rājasya putro vasati putraka
tvām netum āgato vīro yudhājit mātulaḥ tava |
verses.translation: "This is your maternal uncle and the son of king of Kekaya, and this valiant Yudhaajit came here to take you to Kekaya province, and he is staying behind because of your marriage..." thus Dasharatha bade farewell to Bharata suggesting that Bharata may now go with Yudhaajit.

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा दशरथस्यैतद्भरतः कैकेयीसुतः
गमनायाभिचक्राम शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा |
verses.iast:
śrutvā daśarathasya etat bharataḥ kaikeyi sutaḥ
gamanāya abhicakrāma śatrughna sahitaḥ tadā |
verses.translation: On hearing the opinion of Dasharatha, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi, then readied himself to travel along with Shatrughna to Kekaya province.

verses.devanagari:
आपृच्छ्य पितरं शूरो रामं चाक्लिष्टकर्मणम्
मातृश्चापि नरश्रेष्टः शत्रुघ्नसहितो ययौ |
verses.iast:
āpṛcchya pitaram śūro rāmam ca akliṣṭa karmaṇam
mātṝḥ ca api naraśreṣṭa śatrughna sahito yayau |
verses.translation: That valiant and best one among men Bharata on asking leave from his father, from Rama, an uncomplicatedly dextrous one in undertaking deeds, and even from his mothers, Kaikeyi, Sumitra, and Kausalya, travelled on along with Shatrughna.

glosses.meaning: without, complexities, doer of deeds [uncomplicatedly dextrous in deeds]

verses.devanagari:
युधाजित् प्राप्य भरतं सशत्रुघ्नं प्रहर्षितः
स्वपुरं प्राविशद्वीरः पिता तस्य तुतोष ह |
verses.iast:
yudhājit prāpya bharatam sa śatrughnam praharṣitaḥ
sva puram praviveśat vīraḥ pitā tasya tutoṣa ha |
verses.translation: Yudhaajit on clinching not only Bharata, but Shatrughna also, that valiant one is highly gladdened and entered his own city, indeed to the high rejoice of his father, King of Kekaya.

verses.devanagari:
गते च भरते रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः
पितरं देवसंकाशं पूजयामासतुस्तदा |
verses.iast:
gate ca bharate rāmo lakśmaṇaḥ ca mahābalaḥ
pitaram deva saṅkāśam pūjayāmāsatuḥ tadā |
verses.translation: After the departure of Bharata, then the masterly proficient Rama along with Lakshmana started to square with the plans and programs of of his godly father for an ideal-sovereignty.

glosses.meaning: great mighty Rama [here: masterly proficient Rama]

verses.devanagari:
पितुराज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य पौरकार्याणि सर्वशः
चकार रामः सर्वाणि प्रियाणि च हितानि च |
मातृभ्यो मातृकार्याणि कृत्वा परमयंत्रितः
गुरूणां गुरुकार्याणि काले कालेऽन्ववैक्षत |
verses.iast:
pituḥ ājñām puraskṛtya paura kāryāṇi sarvaśaḥ
cakāra rāmaḥ sarvāṇi priyāṇi ca hitāni ca |
mātṛbhyo mātṛ kāryāṇi kṛtvā parama yantritaḥ
gurūṇām guru kāryāṇi kāle kāle anvavaikśata |
verses.translation: Rama keeping his father's directives in view undertook welfare activities for the people that are agreeable and even advantageous to them, and in the entirety of those activities, and he undertook activities to humour motherly affection with his mothers, and educational activities with educators, and in a highly self-disciplined manner he used to review them carefully from time to time.

glosses.meaning: for mothers, mother's, activities [to humour motherly affection]

verses.devanagari:
एवं दशरथः प्रीतो ब्राह्मणा नैगमास्तथा
रामस्य शीलवृत्तेन सर्वं विषयवासिनः |
तेषामतियशा लोके रामः सत्यपराक्रमः
स्वयम्भूरिव भूतानां बभूव गुणवत्तरः |
verses.iast:
evam daśarathaḥ prīto brāhmaṇā naigamāḥ tathā
rāmasya śīla vṛttena sarvam viṣaya vāsinaḥ |
teṣām ati yaśā loke rāmaḥ satya parākramaḥ
svayambhūḥ iva bhūtānām babhūva guṇavattaraḥ |
verses.translation: That way Dasharatha is pleased with the deportment and comportment of Rama, likewise the Brahman-s and urbanites, and even all of the indwellers in the entire kingdom are pleased, and he who has high distinction, his truthfulness alone is his vantage point, and whose hallmarks are of higher degree, that Rama has manifested himself to those subjects in the kingdom, and even to all of the living beings in the world, as the Self-Created Brahma.

glosses.meaning: by hallmarks, higher [in degree, de haut en bas]
truthfulness, being vanquishing point [being vantage point]

verses.devanagari:
रामश्च सीतया सार्धं विजहार बहूनृतून्
मनस्वी तद्गतमानस्य तस्या हृदि समर्पितः |
verses.iast:
rāmaḥ ca sītayā sārdham vijahāra bahūn ṛtūn
manasvī tad gatamānasya tasyā hṛdi samarpitaḥ |
verses.translation: Also, that hearty Rama who permeated into the heart of Seetha is ensconced in Seetha's heart alone, and he disported for many seasons along with Seetha.
notes: The other mms use rāmaḥ tu instead of rāmaḥ ca where this tu says a difference. Then, 'Rama is busy in welfare and other works of state, tu 'but' he is also impassioned for Seetha. And he is manasvī 'hearty one' warm, friendly, spirited etc., are his dispositions for kingdom, people, governmental works tu 'but' he is that 'hearty' for Seetha... Hence tad gataḥ - tasyām gataḥ 'he pervaded her psyche, hence casketed in her heart... In the other mms it will be tasyāḥ hṛdi nityam samarpitaḥ 'heart of Seetha is 'always' dedicated to Rama... and that word nityam 'always, eternal, everlasting...' couple. So, they may be a couple from time immemorial tu 'but' they are as good as a fresh and fervent young couple... bahūn ṛtūn 'for many, many seasons to come...' he is disporting with Seetha. Why tell seasons when there is calculated calendar with years, decades, and centuries... Not so... their disporting is according to seasons, with seasonal environ, with a seasonable togetherness... vijahāra is grammatically a parasmai padi then the fruition goes to the subject, and subject of the verse is Rama, so he alone is the enjoyer and insatiate is his enjoyment with Seetha, even during and after bahūn ṛtūn many, and many seasons. niravadhika paraspara baddha anurāga abhivṛddhi ' an endless, mutual, conjugal, impassion and its enrichment - the self-content bliss of monogamy.

glosses.meaning: her [alone,] one who permeated [into her heart]
in her, in heart, well, dedicated [ensconce in her heart]

verses.devanagari:
प्रिया तु सीता रामस्य दाराः पितृकृता इति
गुणाद्रूपगुणाच्चापि प्रीतिर्भूयोऽभिवर्धते |
verses.iast:
priyā tu sītā rāmasya dārāḥ pitṛ kṛtā iti
guṇāt rūpa guṇāt ca api prītiḥ bhūyo abhivardhate |
verses.translation: Seetha has become the beloved of Rama as she is wedded with the assent of his father Dasharatha, further Rama's love for Seetha burgeoned by virtue of Seetha's own virtues and loveliness.
notes: Here the good old saying ati rūpavatī sītā - ati mūrkhāḥ ca rāvaṇa 'Seetha is the greatest beauty, Ravana is the highest pigheaded demon...' may be remembered. He loved her for his father's voice / Had given her and approved the choice: / He loved her for each charm she wore / And her sweet virtues more and more. - Griffith.

glosses.meaning: comeliness, by virtue of, also, even

verses.devanagari:
तस्याश्च भर्ता द्विगुणं हृदये परिवर्तते
अन्तर्गतमपि व्यक्तमाख्याति हृदयं हृदा |
verses.iast:
tasyāḥ ca bhartā dviguṇam hṛdaye parivar.htate
antar gatam api vyaktam ākhyāti hṛdayam hṛdā |
verses.translation: Even Rama as her husband made his mark in Seetha's heart twice as good, and they both used to clearly converse about their thoughts in their heart of hearts, just by their hearts.

glosses.meaning: two, fold [twice as good,] made his mark
in heart, interior of, went into [thoughts in heart of hearts]

verses.devanagari:
तस्य भूयो विशेषेण मैथिली जनकात्मजा |
देवताभिः समा रूपे सीता श्रीरिव रूपिणी
verses.iast:
tasya bhūyo viśeṣeṇa maithilī janaka ātmajā |
devatābhiḥ samā rūpe sītā śrīḥ iva rūpiṇī
verses.translation: In her mien Seetha is identical with goddesses, and she is like personified Goddess Lakshmi, thus she is the reshaped Divine Prosperity, and as she hails from Holy Mithila she shall be held Holy, and since she is the daughter of Janaka, a loftiest sagacious and invincible king, she is sagely and stately, besides being shapely, and she with all these heaps of natural traits and characteristics, Seetha is rejoicing the heart of Rama. [1-77-28b, c]

glosses.meaning: prosperity, as though, personified, reshaped] maithilii = one from Mithila province [a holy land, hence she is Holy]
Janaka's, soul-born, [daughter of the loftiest sagacious king Janaka]

verses.devanagari:
तया स राजर्षिसुतोऽभिकामया
समेयिवानुत्तमराजकन्यया |
अतीव रामः शुशुभे मुदान्वितो
विभुः श्रिया विष्णुरिवामरेश्वरः
verses.iast:
tayā sa rāja ṛṣi suto abhikāmayā
sameyivān uttama rāja kanyayā |
atīva rāmaḥ śuśubhe mudā anvito
vibhuḥ śriyā viṣṇuḥ iva amara īśvaraḥ
verses.translation: When passionately conjugated with such a princess from the irreproachable king Janaka, Rama, the son of sagely king Dasharatha, has enthusiastically shone forth like the God of Gods and the Efficient Cause, namely Vishnu, when He is together with Goddess Lakshmi.
notes: The 'son of king' suggests that Rama as a prospective king has no paucity for any items of enjoyment. The best 'princess' suggests that Seetha is no less than him, but now her prosperity edges on that of Rama, because she has Rama as her husband. And how will be their mutual affection and love? Many more pages can be written on it, but insufficiently, and perhaps inefficiently. This stanza from a romantic work līnena prati bimbite iva likhite utkīrṇa rūpeva ca | pratyupteva ca vajra lepa ghaṭite iva antar nikhāte iva ca | sā naḥ cetasi kīlitena viśikhaiḥ ceto bhuvaḥ pancabhiḥ | cintā santati tantu jālena nibiḍa syūte iva lagnā priyā || 'my darling is immersed in my heart as sugar merges in milk, as the Red oleander reflects in a prism, as a portrait painted on canvas, as a picture carved on a stone tablet, as a gem studded in a ring, as bedaubed skin-cream, and as though the five darts of Love-god are nailed fixedly, [which darts usually will be in a touch-and-go fashion,] and as though stringed with thought-strings of my heartstrings, that are the halters with fastness...'
